value.name: present memorandum terms
value.description: Asha explains a short memorandum outlining the next steps for the inheritance dispute, including appraisal, inventory, and possible buyout or sale options.
evidence: I have drafted a short document — it is not a contract, it is a memorandum — that lays out a sequence. Independent appraisal. Inventory of contents. A meeting two weeks from today at which any one of you may exercise the right of first refusal under the codicil, or all three of you may elect to sell, or any two of you may buy out the third, or you may agree to defer the decision for an additional thirty days.

value.name: request review without signature
value.description: Asha asks the others to read the memorandum and says she does not need a signature today, only their willingness to review it.
evidence: I would like to walk through the memorandum with you and then leave it on the table for the rest of the day. I do not need a signature today. I need only your willingness to read it.

value.name: distribute memorandum copies
value.description: Asha slides three copies of the memorandum across the table to the three family members.
evidence: She slid three copies across the table.

value.name: Daniel accepts memorandum
value.description: Daniel takes his copy of the memorandum.

value.name: Lucia accepts memorandum
value.description: Lucia takes her copy of the memorandum.

value.name: Rosa hesitates before taking memorandum
value.description: Rosa hesitates over the copy before pulling it toward herself cautiously with two fingers.
evidence: Rosa looked at hers for a moment without touching it, then drew it toward her with two fingers, as if testing whether it was hot.

value.name: family reads memorandum
value.description: Daniel, Lucia, and Rosa begin reading the memorandum while Asha observes them.
evidence: Asha watched them read without watching them read.

value.name: Daniel reads quickly
value.description: Asha notices Daniel reading quickly, partly from habit and partly to preserve his sense of primacy.
evidence: Daniel read fast. He had always read fast, she suspected, and he was reading fast now partly out of habit and partly out of the need to be seen reading fast, to be the first one finished, to retain some small primacy in a room in which his primacy had been considerably reduced.

value.name: Lucia reads carefully
value.description: Asha observes Lucia reading slowly, revisiting phrases and silently mouthing technical terms.
evidence: Lucia read slowly, going back over phrases, her lips moving very faintly on the technical terms.

value.name: Rosa reads formal English cautiously
value.description: Asha notices Rosa reading at the pace of someone unaccustomed to formal English.
evidence: Rosa read at the pace of a woman who had not been asked, often, to read formal Englis
